title: CompoDistill: Attention Distillation for Compositional Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs
claim: Distilled student models fail to close the compositional-reasoning gap to the teacher because their visual attention is misaligned with the teacher's, while ours narrows it.
layout: 2 panels side by side: (a) scatter plot with size-encoded markers and gap arrows, (b) query text above input photo and student/teacher attention heatmaps
description: Two panels. Panel (a) is a scatter plot with VQA performance on the x-axis and compositional-reasoning (CR) performance on the y-axis. Colored circles mark the teacher (blue), an SFT model (orange), LLaVA-KD (green), LLaVADI (purple) and LLaVA-MoD (pink). Circle size encodes training-set size (1.2M, 1.5M, 5.0M). The red star labelled CompoDistill (Ours) sits well above the baselines and closest to the teacher. A dashed diagonal line runs through the plot. Blue and red arrows show the VQA gains and the 'No Improvement in CR' gap between baselines and the teacher. Panel (b) shows a person icon and the speech-box query 'A woman is on the table.' Below it are a photo of a woman standing on a table and two attention heatmap overlays. The green-framed student (LLaVA-KD-2B) heatmap is scattered over irrelevant regions. The blue-framed teacher (LLaVA-4B) heatmap focuses on the woman and the table.
caption: (a) Comparison of the teacher (LLaVA-4B), SFT (LLaVA-2B), and various 2B KD methods distilled from the same teacher. (b) Visual attention misalignment between the student (LLaVA-KD-2B) and teacher (LLaVA-4B), where the student attends to irrelevant image regions for the text query A woman is on the table, in contrast to the teacher. {For more examples including our proposed method, \proposed{}, please refer to Appendix [ref]}.
abstract: Recently, efficient Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have gained significant attention as a solution to their high computational complexity, making them more practical for real-world applications. In this regard, the knowledge distillation (KD) approach has emerged as a promising alternative, which transfers the rich visual and linguistic knowledge from a larger model (teacher) to a smaller model (student). However, we observe that existing KD methods struggle to effectively distill the teacher MLLM's rich visual perception abilities to the student, a challenge that has been largely overlooked in previous studies. Through a systematic analysis, we identify visual attention misalignment between student and teacher as the main cause of this issue. Based on this insight, we propose CompoDistill, a novel KD framework that explicitly aligns the student's visual attention with that of the teacher to enhance the student's visual perception abilities. Our extensive experiments show that CompoDistill significantly improves performance on compositional reasoning tasks that require visual perception abilities while maintaining strong performance on visual question answering tasks, as done in existing studies. Furthermore, CompoDistill demonstrates effectiveness with a more advanced backbone, highlighting its generalizability.
